title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - SummitCloud
next_steps: Evelyn to send updated pricing for Dedicated + multi-region add-on
Samir to schedule throughput benchmark and provide test plan
SummitCloud to share traffic profile and 99th percentile latency SLOs
Priya to share contract redlines and procurement timeline
action_items: Evelyn Park: Send updated pricing for Dedicated capacity + multi-region option (due 2026-09-14)
Samir Patel: Schedule benchmark window and run 24h stress test; share test plan (due 2026-09-18)
Rachel Kim: Provide current traffic profile (qps, burst patterns) and 99th latency SLOs (due 2026-09-13)
Priya Singh: Share draft contract redlines and procurement timeline (due 2026-09-20)
header: Attendees: Evelyn Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Rachel Kim, Derek Holt, Priya Singh (SummitCloud)
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on upgrading to Dedicated capacity, adding EU region, and aligning on contract extension timing. Customer requests benchmarks and security docs before committing to multi-region add-on.
topics: Current usage and fit with Dedicated vs hosted
Pricing for reserved capacity and burst policies
transcript: [00:00] Evelyn Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check in for renewal and expansion — we have about 45 minutes, we'll cover dedicated capacity, EU region, and next steps
[00:12] Rachel Kim: Sounds good. just a quick heads up, we've seen a 2.5x qps increase month over month, so main ask is how Dedicated would handle bursty inference and multi-region routing

[00:22] Samir Patel: Cool, thanks Rachel. we looked at your traffic from the last 30 days and the patterns — Ded pool sizing we recommended in the deck should handle steady state but we need to size for spikes, that's where burst capacity comes in
[00:33] Derek Holt: On burst, how quickly can you spin up GPUs in another region? we have EU users and need data residency for some customers

[00:44] Samir Patel: We can pre-reserve a pool in eu-west and enable cross-region routing. in practice warmup is near instant for cold starts if KV cache is primed, but full node spin-up can take a few minutes unless you use reserved burst nodes
[01:02] Rachel Kim: When you say KV, do you mean KV cache? we've seen sometimes the transcriptions call it KV cash hehe — also, any specifics on 99th percentile latency after quantization?

[01:15] Samir Patel: yes KV cache — sorry, transcriber typo. for your 99th percentile, based on our tests with the model family you're using, Dedicated with n1 quant profile hits about 120-150ms p99 per token in eu config, but we'll verify with your prompt mix
[01:32] Priya Singh: From procurement side, timeline is tight — we need pricing and SOC2/ISO docs to move budget next week

[01:40] Evelyn Park: Understood. I'll get updated pricing for the Dedicated commit and the multi-region add-on. We'll include optional burst pricing and estimated monthly cost. We'll also share SOC2 + ISO and our KMS/HSM integration note
[01:55] Derek Holt: Curious about encryption — if we bring our own KMS, how does key rotation and audit logs look? we need audit trails for a couple of customers

[02:05] Samir Patel: We support customer-managed keys via KMS; rotation policy is configurable and audit logs are delivered to your logging bucket. We'll attach the integration guide. note: in private deployments we can do HSM if needed
[02:18] Rachel Kim: Great. On the benchmarking front, we need a test that reflects our bursty traffic: spikes to 3x baseline for 15 minutes every 3 hours. can Redwood simulate that in the pilot?
[02:33] Samir Patel: Yep — we can run a stress run and simulate your qps pattern. we'll need a test window and access to a staging API key, and ideally a sample prompt set and token distributions
[02:45] Rachel Kim: I'll send prompt sets and token distributions — a mix of short and long prompts. expect some noisy transcriber text in the upload names haha
[02:55] Priya Singh: On contract length, what's typical? We were thinking 12 months but want option to extend with a better rate after 6 months if metrics are met

[03:07] Evelyn Park: We generally do 12- or 24-month reserved commits. We can offer mid-term repricing after a 6-month review tied to metrics (latency, availability, usage). I'll draft language for a contract extension clause
[03:18] Derek Holt: Any limitations for VPC/private deploy vs hosted? We might need a private control plane for some regulated customers

[03:27] Samir Patel: Private option gives you a customer-managed control plane and network isolation. It requires extra lead time for deployment and connectivity, but meets higher compliance needs. For your immediate needs, Dedicated in-region with VPC peering can be a good stopgap
[03:40] Rachel Kim: About model fallbacks — if we go with a smaller quantized variant during spikes, how transparent is the routing and what are the quality tradeoffs?

[03:50] Samir Patel: Good question. routing policies can be automated: route by latency or cost and fallback to a compatible variant if capacity is constrained. quality regressions are model-specific; we'll run eval prompts and measure hallucination / rouge-like metrics as part of the pilot
[04:05] Evelyn Park: Also, we'll surface the Optimize suggestions for batching/caching; sometimes a few prompt engineering tweaks dramatically reduce token usage and cost
[04:15] Rachel Kim: Sounds helpful. We'll want to see a cost run-rate with and without batching optimizations
[04:24] Priya Singh: For procurement, is there a standard SOW? we need deliverables and acceptance criteria for the pilot

[04:33] Evelyn Park: Yes, we'll include a pilot SOW: scope (benchmark goals), acceptance criteria (p99 < target, throughput), duration (2 weeks), and handoff plan. Samir will propose the technical test plan
[04:45] Samir Patel: I'll send the test plan with steps, metrics to capture, and required creds. we'll propose two benchmark windows next week and aim for the 24h stress run
[04:58] Derek Holt: One more on monitoring — can we get per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdowns in the console? we need to map cost to teams
[05:08] Samir Patel: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route cost and latency breakdowns, and tracing hooks. We can demo that during the pilot and give access to a manager role
[05:18] Rachel Kim: Any blockers from our side aside from the prompt set and traffic profile?
[05:24] Priya Singh: Contract side — we'll need the SOC2 and the standard procurement paperwork. also internal legal will want the data residency assurances for the EU region
[05:34] Evelyn Park: We'll attach SOC2/ISO docs and a short note on data residency and routing rules. also, I'll include the KMS integration doc and the audit log sample
[05:45] Rachel Kim: Regarding cost — can you provide an example monthly estimate for our current baseline and the recommended Dedicated config? we want to compare hosted vs reserved
[05:54] Evelyn Park: I'll put together a cost comparison sheet with assumptions and a worked example. will include per-token delta for batching on/off and estimated savings with prefix caching
[06:05] Samir Patel: Note on benchmarking: we should run with your real prompt set to capture tokenization differences; synthetic tests often understate costs
[06:14] Rachel Kim: Agree. I'll deliver the prompt set today. also want to confirm SLA targets — our customers expect 99.95% availability
[06:24] Evelyn Park: Our Dedicated SLA covers 99.9% by default; we can discuss 99.95% as part of an enterprise SLA add-on. I'll include SLA options in the pricing doc
[06:36] Priya Singh: Timeline recap: procurement decision targeted for 2026-09-24. is that doable if we get pricing and SOC2 by 09-14?
[06:45] Evelyn Park: That's doable. We'll prioritize sending pricing and security docs by 09-14 so you can start internal reviews
[06:55] Samir Patel: I'll also propose benchmark windows for 09-16 and 09-17. if that works for you, we'll run the stress test on 09-18 as a follow-up
[07:05] Rachel Kim: 09-16/17 works. quick note — our QA team will want a read-only view into the console during the pilot
[07:12] Evelyn Park: Noted, we'll provision a read-only role for QA. we'll also give access to trace and cost dashboards
[07:22] Priya Singh: Ok, thanks everyone. any final concerns?
[07:27] Derek Holt: No, just want to make sure the contract language around data residency is explicit
[07:31] Evelyn Park: We'll draft that clause and circulate. quick recap of action items and owners after the call

[07:38] Evelyn Park: (recap) Evelyn to send pricing, SOC2/ISO, SOW and cost sheet by 2026-09-14. Samir to send test plan and schedule benchmarks (due 2026-09-18). Rachel to send prompts and traffic profile by EOD. Priya to share procurement timing and redlines by 2026-09-20
[07:58] Rachel Kim: Thanks all, appreciated. talk soon
[08:01] Evelyn Park: Thanks everybody, we'll follow up by email and post the docs in the shared drive
